 260			}
 261	
 262			if res == resContinuation {
 263				if !c.PrefillSupported {
 264					term = resOutputExhausted
 265					break
 266				}
 267				continuations++
 268				if continuations > continuationCap {
 269					term = resOutputExhausted // cap hit
 270					break
 271				}
 272				// Stitch: accumulated + current partial becomes the prefill.
 273				c.multiResponseContent += c.partialResponseContent
 274				if n := len(messages); n > 0 && messages[n-1].Role == "assistant" {
 275					messages[n-1] = llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent)
 276				} else {
 277					messages = append(messages, llm.TextMessage("assistant", c.multiResponseContent))
 278				}
 279				continue
 280			}
 281	
 282			term = res // resDone, resInterrupted, resLooping, resContextExhausted
 283			break
 284		}
 285		interrupted := term == resInterrupted
 286	
 287		// --- Finally (always runs) ---
 288		c.Out.FlushStream()
 289		answer := c.multiResponseContent + c.partialResponseContent
 290		answer = stripReasoning(answer, c.Model.ReasoningTag)
 291		c.partialResponseContent = answer
 292		c.multiResponseContent = ""
 293	
 294		// --- Post-stream dispatch ---
 295		c.finalizeUsage(usage)
 296	
 297		if answer != "" || len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 298			msg := llm.TextMessage("assistant", answer)
 299			if len(c.partialToolCalls) > 0 {
 300				msg.ToolCalls = c.partialToolCalls
 301			}
 302			c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, msg)
 303		}
 304	
 305		// dropUserTurn un-appends the user message this send added, so a send that
 306		// produced nothing doesn't poison the history. It is a no-op on a tool
 307		// continuation, which appended no user turn — truncating there would drop a
 308		// tool result and leave a tool_call unanswered, making the next request
 309		// malformed.
 310		dropUserTurn := func() {
 311			if appendedUser {
 312				c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:len(c.curMessages)-1]
 313			}
 314		}
 315	
 316		switch term {
 317		case resContextExhausted:
 318			// A system message, not an assistant one. The model did not say this —
 319			// the request never reached a reply — so putting it in the assistant's
 320			// voice fabricates a turn, and one in which the model appears to report
 321			// its own transport error. The note exists so the next request does not
 322			// end on a bare user turn with no answer, which is what the role check
 323			// below is for; whose voice carries it is a separate question, and the
 324			// harness's own is the honest one.
 325			if n := len(c.curMessages); n > 0 && c.curMessages[n-1].Role == "user" {
 326				c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages,
 327					llm.TextMessage(llm.RoleSystem, "The reply was cut off: the request exceeded the context limit."))
 328			}
 329			c.showExhaustedError()
 330			return OutcomeContextExhausted, ""
 331		case resOutputExhausted:
 332			// The large partial was kept above; no diagnostic (trailing message
 333			// is the assistant partial).
 334			return OutcomeOutputExhausted, ""
 335		case resFailed:
 336			if answer == "" {
 337				dropUserTurn()
 338			}
 339			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 340		case resLooping:
 341			// The user turn stays. Unlike an empty reply, this one produced
 342			// something — it produced too much of one thing — and the note below
 343			// only makes sense following the message it answers.
 344			c.warnLoop(loops.Found)
 345			c.noteLoop(loops.Found)
 346			return OutcomeLooping, ""
 347		}
 348	
 349		if !interrupted && answer == "" && len(c.partialToolCalls) == 0 {
 350			dropUserTurn()
 351			c.Out.Warningf("Empty response received from LLM. Check your provider account?")
 352			return OutcomeFailed, ""
 353		}
 354	
 355		if interrupted {
 356			c.noteInterrupt()
 357			return OutcomeInterrupted, ""
 358		}
 359	
 360		// Everything a turn does now arrives as tool calls, in every mode: ask mode
 361		// is the same dispatch with the mutating tools withheld. There is no longer
 362		// a second path that reads the answer text for edits, shell blocks, or file
 363		// mentions — those were the text formats' way of saying what a tool call
 364		// says directly.
 365		return c.applyToolCalls(ctx), ""
 366	}

 368	// noteInterrupt records that the human stopped the reply, in a shape the next
 369	// request can be built from.
 370	//
 371	// Two things it deliberately does not do, both of which it used to.
 372	//
 373	// It does not put words in the model's mouth. The old shape appended an
 374	// assistant turn saying "I see that you interrupted my previous reply", which
 375	// the model never said; the harness's own voice is the honest one, and the rest
 376	// of this file already says so about the context-exhausted note.
 377	//
 378	// It does not edit "^C KeyboardInterrupt" into the user's own message. Whatever
 379	// the human typed is what the human typed. assemble.go makes the same argument
 380	// about the system reminder, and this was the last place still doing it.
 381	//
 382	// The partial reply itself stays. It is real output the model produced, and
 383	// keeping it is what makes "continue as before" continue rather than restart.
 384	// Its *tool calls* do not stay — see dropPartialToolCalls.
 385	func (c *Coder) noteInterrupt() {
 386		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 387		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 388			"The user pressed Ctrl-C, so your reply above was cut off where it stops. "+
 389				"Anything you were part-way through saying was not finished, and any tool "+
 390				"call you had begun was not run — nothing it would have changed has changed."))
 391	}

 393	// warnLoop tells the user what the model was doing when it was stopped, in
 394	// every mode: script runs have no steer menu, and a run that stopped early is
 395	// the one thing a log must not be silent about.
 396	func (c *Coder) warnLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 397		if f == nil {
 398			c.Out.Warningf("The model's reply was repeating itself, so it was stopped.")
 399			return
 400		}
 401		c.Out.Warningf("The model's %s was repeating itself (%q %d times), so it was stopped.",
 402			f.Kind, f.Sample, f.Count)
 403	}

 405	// noteLoop records that the harness stopped a reply that was repeating itself.
 406	//
 407	// In the harness's own voice, for the same reason as noteInterrupt: nobody
 408	// pressed Ctrl-C, and saying the user did would be a fabrication about the one
 409	// participant whose actions the model cannot check.
 410	//
 411	// It quotes the repeating text back. A model given "you were repeating
 412	// yourself" and nothing else has to guess which part, and the guess is often
 413	// the whole reply; the sample makes the instruction actionable.
 414	func (c *Coder) noteLoop(f *loopFinding) {
 415		c.dropPartialToolCalls()
 416		where := "reply"
 417		if f != nil && f.Kind == loopReasoning {
 418			where = "reasoning"
 419		}
 420		note := "Strument stopped your " + where + " because it had begun repeating itself"
 421		if f != nil {
 422			note += fmt.Sprintf(" — %q appeared %d times", f.Sample, f.Count)
 423		}
 424		note += ". Nothing you were part-way through was finished, and any tool call " +
 425			"you had begun was not run. Do not continue that text or write it again: " +
 426			"take a different approach, and if you are stuck, say so plainly and stop."
 427		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(note))
 428	}

 430	// noteToolInterrupt records a Ctrl-C that landed while a tool was running.
 431	//
 432	// Distinct from noteInterrupt, which describes a *stream* cut off mid-word and
 433	// says any tool call the model had begun was never run. Here the opposite is
 434	// true: the calls ran, their results are in the history, and one of them was
 435	// stopped part-way. Telling the model the other story would have it repeat work
 436	// that already happened, or distrust a result that is real.
 437	func (c *Coder) noteToolInterrupt() {
 438		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 439		c.curMessages = append(c.curMessages, llm.HarnessNote(
 440			"The user pressed Ctrl-C while your tool calls were running. Their results "+
 441				"above are real as far as they got, and a command that was stopped says so "+
 442				"in its own output. Nothing after the interruption ran."))
 443	}

 445	// dropPartialToolCalls strips tool calls from the assistant message an
 446	// interrupted send just appended.
 447	//
 448	// Not tidiness — correctness. An unanswered tool_call makes the *next* request
 449	// malformed, and after an interrupt no result will ever answer one: the call is
 450	// either half-streamed and unparseable, or complete but never dispatched,
 451	// because the interrupt landed before applyToolCalls ran. Either way the model
 452	// must be told it did not happen, which the note above does, rather than shown
 453	// a call it may assume succeeded.
 454	//
 455	// The message's text survives. Only an assistant message can carry tool calls,
 456	// so this looks at one message and only when it is the last.
 457	func (c *Coder) dropPartialToolCalls() {
 458		c.partialToolCalls = nil
 459		n := len(c.curMessages)
 460		if n == 0 {
 461			return
 462		}
 463		last := &c.curMessages[n-1]
 464		if last.Role != llm.RoleAssistant || len(last.ToolCalls) == 0 {
 465			return
 466		}
 467		if last.Text() == "" {
 468			// Nothing but the abandoned calls: drop the whole turn rather than
 469			// leave an empty assistant message in the history.
 470			c.curMessages = c.curMessages[:n-1]
 471			return
 472		}
 473		last.ToolCalls = nil
 474	}

 476	// buildRequest translates state into an llm.Request.
 477	func (c *Coder) buildRequest(messages []llm.Message) llm.Request {
 478		req := llm.Request{
 479			Model:           c.Model.Slug,
 480			Messages:        messages,
 481			Temperature:     c.Model.Temperature,
 482			ReasoningEffort: c.Model.Reasoning,
 483			ExtraParams:     c.Model.RequestExtraParams(),
 484		}
 485		// Whatever tools this mode offers, offer them. The condition used to be
 486		// editFormat == "tool", which meant ask mode sent none at all — and made
 487		// toolDefs's own "ask" branch unreachable, so the code read as though ask
 488		// had a read-only tool set while the wire carried nothing. A model told to
 489		// look at the project with no way to do it invents the syntax: MiMo emitted
 490		// <bash>ls -la</bash> as prose, and one run spent 759 lines guessing at
 491		// markup. RunAside builds its own request and is deliberately not affected.
 492		if defs := c.toolDefs(); len(defs) > 0 {
 493			req.Tools = defs
 494			req.ToolChoice = "auto"
 495		}
 496		return req
 497	}

 499	// CheckRestoredContext warns if what a session *starts* with already overruns
 500	// the declared window.
 501	//
 502	// Restored context is invisible until the first request, and by then the request
 503	// has failed. aider #2979 is the shape: an 80k-token restored history fails on
 504	// the wire, and configuring the side model for summarization does not help,
 505	// because compaction runs at the end of a turn and there has not been one yet.
 506	// Strument restores less — pins, notes, and the read-only block rather than a
 507	// conversation — but the same trap is available, and a user who pinned a large
 508	// spec last session should hear about it before typing rather than after.
 509	//
 510	// It warns rather than asking. A confirmation before the user has typed
 511	// anything is a toll on every start, and there is nothing to decide yet: the
 512	// remedy is /drop or /notes drop, which they can reach either way.
 513	func (c *Coder) CheckRestoredContext() {
 514		if c.Model == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 515			return
 516		}
 517		n := c.countMessages(c.formatMessages().allMessages()) + c.countTools()
 518		if n < c.Model.Context {
 519			return
 520		}
 521		c.Out.Warningf("This session starts with about %d tokens of context, which already reaches "+
 522			"the %d-token limit for %s.", n, c.Model.Context, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 523		c.Out.Printf("Use /drop to unpin files, /notes drop to discard the session notes, or /tokens to see the split.")
 524	}

 526	// checkTokens warns when the estimate reaches the input window and asks to
 527	// proceed.
 528	func (c *Coder) checkTokens(messages []llm.Message) bool {
 529		maxInput := c.Model.Context
 530		if maxInput <= 0 {
 531			return true
 532		}
 533		// The schemas count: they go out with this request like everything else,
 534		// and leaving them out made the guard cheerful about a prompt 1.3k tokens
 535		// closer to the limit than it reported.
 536		inputTokens := c.countMessages(messages) + c.countTools()
 537		if inputTokens < maxInput {
 538			return true
 539		}
 540		c.Out.Errorf("Your estimated chat context of %d tokens exceeds the %d token limit for %s!",
 541			inputTokens, maxInput, c.Model.QualifiedSlug())
 542		c.Out.Printf("To reduce the chat context:")
 543		c.Out.Printf("- Use /drop to remove unneeded files from the chat")
 544		c.Out.Printf("- Use /clear to clear the chat history")
 545		c.Out.Printf("- Break your code into smaller files")
 546		c.Out.Printf("It's probably safe to try and send the request, most providers won't charge if the context limit is exceeded.")
 547		res := c.Confirm.Confirm(ConfirmRequest{Prompt: "Try to proceed anyway?", Grant: GrantContext})
 548		return res.Yes
 549	}

 551	// moveBackCurMessages rotates cur into done on edited turns.
 552	//
 553	// aider appended a synthetic "I applied and committed your changes" user turn
 554	// here, plus an "Ok." from the assistant, because with SEARCH/REPLACE there was
 555	// no other channel: a text edit format has nothing to answer the model with.
 556	// The tool loop has one. Every edit call already gets a tool result saying what
 557	// it did to which file, so the pair would only repeat it — two fabricated
 558	// messages per turn, in a loop whose whole correction was to stop inventing
 559	// turns the model never took. The commit is reported to the user instead, where
 560	// the hash is worth something.
 561	func (c *Coder) moveBackCurMessages() {
 562		c.doneMessages = append(c.doneMessages, c.curMessages...)
 563		c.curMessages = nil
 564		c.recordedMessages = 0
 565		c.maybeSummarize()
 566	}

 568	// endTurnHistory settles the finished turn and compacts if it has outgrown the
 569	// budget. Called once from runOne's defer, after the commit and the snapshot.
 570	//
 571	// It used to be gated on `editFormat == "tool" && len(turnEditedFiles) > 0`, so
 572	// only a turn that changed a file produced any settled history at all. A live
 573	// pass found what that costs: a session of questions, or any stretch of /ask,
 574	// kept everything in curMessages — which goes on the wire in full and which
 575	// maybeSummarize never examines — so the history budget existed and nothing was
 576	// ever measured against it.
 577	//
 578	// The gate is a vestige. In aider the rotation carried a synthetic "I applied
 579	// and committed your changes" pair, which only made sense after an edit;
 580	// moveBackCurMessages's own comment records removing the pair, and the gate
 581	// stayed behind. What genuinely must not happen is rotating *mid-loop*, where
 582	// compaction would eat the tool results the next send reacts to — and that is
 583	// enforced by this running in the turn-end defer, not by asking what the turn
 584	// did.
 585	//
 586	// Rotation does not move anything on the wire: done and cur are adjacent and
 587	// both sit after the read-only block, so the split is bookkeeping. What changes
 588	// is that compaction can now see the conversation.
 589	func (c *Coder) endTurnHistory() {
 590		if len(c.curMessages) == 0 {
 591			return
 592		}
 593		c.moveBackCurMessages()
 594	}

 606		for _, m := range msgs {

 614	func validCompaction(msgs []llm.Message, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens int) bool {
 615		return len(msgs) < beforeMessages && afterTokens < beforeTokens && hasSummaryContent(msgs)
 616	}

 618	func hasSummaryContent(msgs []llm.Message) bool {
 619		for _, m := range msgs {
 620			if isSummaryMessage(m) && strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(m.Text(), summaryPrefix)) != "" {
 621				return true
 622			}
 623		}
 624		return false

 627	// budget. It runs only when a summarizer is wired and the model's window is
 628	// known (Context > 0) — mirroring checkTokens, which treats an unknown window
 629	// as "no limit to enforce". Synchronous: the side-model call happens here,
 630	// before the next prompt is assembled. On failure the history is left intact.
 631	func (c *Coder) maybeSummarize() {
 632		if c.Summarizer == nil || c.Model.Context <= 0 {
 633			return
 634		}
 635		budget := maxChatHistoryTokens(c.Model.Context)
 636		if !c.Summarizer.tooBig(c.doneMessages, budget) {
 637			return
 638		}
 639		if c.summaryBackoff {
 640			c.summaryBackoff = false
 641			return
 642		}
 643		c.Out.Printf("Summarizing chat history to fit the context window...")
 644		beforeTokens := c.Summarizer.total(c.doneMessages)
 645		beforeMessages := len(c.doneMessages)
 646		out, err := c.Summarizer.summarize(c.doneMessages, budget)
 647		if err != nil {
 648			c.summaryBackoff = true
 649			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: %v", err)
 650			return
 651		}
 652		afterTokens := c.Summarizer.total(out)
 653		if !validCompaction(out, beforeTokens, beforeMessages, afterTokens) {
 654			c.summaryBackoff = true
 655			c.Out.Warningf("Could not summarize chat history: the result was not smaller than the original history")
 656			return
 657		}
 658		c.doneMessages = out
 659		c.Out.Printf("Chat history compacted: %d tokens/%s -> %d tokens/%s; %s retained.",
 660			beforeTokens, plural(beforeMessages, "message", "messages"),
 661			afterTokens, plural(len(out), "message", "messages"),
 662			plural(countSummaryMessages(out), "summary", "summaries"))
 663	}

 665	// finalizeUsage resolves cost — (1) in-band cost, (2) config
 666	// pricing, (3) tokens only, never a fabricated $0 — merges into session
 667	// totals, and emits the immutable report. Idempotent; also deferred so a
 668	// mid-send panic can't lose accounting.
 669	func (c *Coder) finalizeUsage(u *sendUsage) {
 670		if u.finalized {
 671			return
 672		}
 673		u.finalized = true
 674	
 675		// prompt_tokens is the whole prompt. Both cache figures live under
 676		// prompt_tokens_details and are a *breakdown* of it, not additions to it:
 677		// on a cold request with a breakpoint, OpenRouter returns
 678		// prompt_tokens=14021, cache_write_tokens=14018, and
 679		// total_tokens=14026 = prompt + completion. Adding the write on top counted
 680		// most of the prompt twice, and only on models that write a cache — which
 681		// is why GPT-5.6 Luna looked like it was sending an order of magnitude more
 682		// than Haiku for the same work. Cache reads were already treated as the
 683		// subset they are; the two are the same kind of number.
 684		sent := u.prompt
 685		received := u.completion
 686		estimated := false
 687	
 688		// A request the provider refused outright — a bad key, a model slug that
 689		// does not exist, an account out of credit — was not processed: no usage,
 690		// no reply, nothing billed. Estimating it printed
 691		//
 692		//	Tokens: 735 sent, 0 received. (estimated)
 693		//
 694		// under a 401, which reads as a charge for the failure. Returning before
 695		// the counters means messageSends stays 0 and flushTurnUsage says nothing
 696		// at all, which is the honest report.
 697		//
 698		// A stream that produced text before it broke is a different case: those
 699		// tokens were generated and will be billed, so it still estimates below.
 700		if u.rejected && sent == 0 && received == 0 && !u.costKnown && c.streamedText() == "" {
 701			return
 702		}
 703	
 704		// No usage arrived — the turn was aborted before the provider's final
 705		// usage chunk (or the provider sends none). The request still went out
 706		// and may have streamed a partial reply, so report our own estimate
 707		// instead of a misleading zero, and mark it so a guess is never shown as
 708		// the provider's ground truth.
 709		if sent == 0 && received == 0 && !u.costKnown && (u.estSent > 0 || c.streamedText() != "") {
 710			estimated = true
 711			sent = u.estSent
 712			received = c.Tokens.Count(c.streamedText())
 713		}
 714	
 715		// Accumulate into the turn rather than assign: a turn is many sends, and the
 716		// line that reports it is printed once, at the end.
 717		c.messageSends++
 718		c.messageTokensSent += sent
 719		c.messageTokensReceived += received
 720		c.messageCacheRead += u.cacheRead
 721		c.messageCacheWrite += u.cacheWrite
 722		c.messageEstimated = c.messageEstimated || estimated
 723		c.totalTokensSent += sent
 724		c.totalTokensReceived += received
 725		c.peakTokensSent = max(c.peakTokensSent, sent)
 726	
 727		report := formatTokenLine(sent, u.cacheWrite, u.cacheRead, received)
 728	
 729		cost := 0.0
 730		known := false
 731		switch {
 732		case u.costKnown:
 733			cost = u.cost
 734			known = true
 735		case c.Model.InputCost != nil && c.Model.OutputCost != nil:
 736			pin := c.Model.InputCost.USD
 737			pout := c.Model.OutputCost.USD
 738			if estimated {
 739				cost = float64(sent)*pin + float64(received)*pout
 740			} else {
 741				// Anthropic-style cache pricing adjustments; no-ops at zero counts
 742				// (DeepSeek's cache-read discount uses the same 0.10 factor). The
 743				// cache figures are carved *out* of the prompt rather than added to
 744				// it — see sent above — so each token is priced exactly once, at
 745				// whichever rate applies to it. Charging them on top of a full-price
 746				// prompt was the same double-count the token line had.
 747				full := max(u.prompt-u.cacheWrite-u.cacheRead, 0)
 748				cost = float64(u.cacheWrite)*pin*1.25 +
 749					float64(u.cacheRead)*pin*0.10 +
 750					float64(full)*pin +
 751					float64(u.completion)*pout
 752			}
 753			known = true
 754		}
 755	
 756		if known {
 757			c.messageCost += cost
 758			c.totalCost += cost
 759			c.costKnown = true
 760			c.sessionKnown = true
 761			report += fmt.Sprintf(" Cost: $%s message, $%s session.", formatCost(cost), formatCost(c.totalCost))
 762		}
 763		if estimated {
 764			report += " (estimated)"
 765		}
 766	
 767		c.lastUsageReport = report
 768	}

 793		cost float64, costKnown bool, totalCost float64, estimated bool,
 794	) string {
